chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from 'Ali from Abu Basir said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the price of a hunting dog. He said, 'There is no objection to its price, but the price of the other is not permissible.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the price of a hunting dog?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the commercial validity of a hunting dog’s price and that of another type of dog, likely referring to the dog of the eater (*kalb al-akl*) whose price is impermissible (*la yahlithu*). This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that while hunting dogs are useful and their trade is valid, the dog of the eater is considered more impure or less utilitarian in a way that affects the permissibility of its sale price, aligning with the broader principle that utility (*manfa'a*) influences commercial validity in Islamic law.
